title: She Took Five for Ten and Became the Leading Wicket-Taker in Women’s T20I History. Deepti Sharma Just Demolished Pakistan at Edgbaston.
excerpt: Smriti Mandhana’s 68 off 44 balls powered India to 170 — their highest-ever T20I total against Pakistan — before Deepti’s career-best spell bowled the opposition out for 106
body:
The numbers alone told the story. Five wickets for ten runs in four overs. A career-best that also carried a milestone no Indian cricketer — man or woman — had reached before in this format. On a turning Edgbaston pitch on Sunday, Deepti Sharma dismantled Pakistan's batting lineup with such clinical efficiency that the contest was effectively over before the 13th over of the chase.

India's Women's T20 World Cup campaign opened with a 64-run demolition of Pakistan, the kind of statement that travels well beyond Birmingham. The reigning 50-over world champions are now chasing the one ICC trophy that has eluded Harmanpreet Kaur's generation, and this was precisely the sort of start they needed in a tournament where Group A is being called the group of death.

## Mandhana sets the platform

India did not have it easy at the start. Shafali Verma launched the very first ball for a maximum, but Sadia Iqbal struck back to remove her for 6. Jemimah Rodrigues lasted just seven balls before falling to Tasmia Rubab. At 18 for 2 inside four overs, the pressure was real.

Smriti Mandhana, as she so often does, absorbed it. She steadied the innings alongside captain Harmanpreet Kaur, and the pair stitched together a 91-run partnership for the third wicket that swung the momentum decisively. Mandhana reached her half-century in 34 balls, shimmying down the track to launch Rubab over long-off for one of two sixes. She finished with 68 off 44 balls — nine fours and two sixes — and was reprieved twice by dropped catches, chances Pakistan could ill afford to waste.

Harmanpreet contributed a composed 36 from 35 balls, and it was Richa Ghosh who provided the late acceleration, smashing 34 off just 17 deliveries to lift India to 170 for 6. That total was India's highest ever against Pakistan in women's T20I cricket — a record that had stood since the 2023 World Cup in Cape Town.

## Deepti's historic spell

The chase began promisingly enough for Pakistan. Muneeba Ali looked fluent, taking the score to 52 for 1 at the end of the powerplay. But the moment Deepti Sharma was introduced, the complexion of the innings changed entirely.

The off-spinner extracted grip and turn from a used Edgbaston surface, consistently finding the outside edge and the pad. Muneeba, who had been Pakistan's best batter with 41 off 35 balls, was run out by a direct hit from Deepti herself — a moment that symbolised how completely the all-rounder controlled proceedings. Pakistan slumped from 52 for 1 to 79 for 6 within the space of seven overs.

Deepti's final figures — 5 for 10 in four overs — were her best in T20 internationals, and they carried her past the previous record for the most wickets in women's T20I history. She was named Player of the Match, her second individual honour in successive ICC tournaments after being named Player of the Tournament at last year's ODI World Cup.

Left-arm spinner Shree Charani provided excellent support with 3 for 21, and Pakistan were eventually bowled out for 106 in 17 overs.

## What it means for NRIs watching from abroad

For the millions of Indian diaspora fans tracking the tournament from living rooms in New Jersey, Hounslow, and Brampton, this was exactly the kind of dominant performance that fuels WhatsApp group celebrations. India vs Pakistan, regardless of format or gender, generates massive viewership across overseas streaming platforms, and a 64-run margin leaves no room for debate.

More importantly, this Indian team is no longer a sentimental favourite. The Women's Premier League has professionalised the domestic pipeline; players like Mandhana and Deepti are now year-round athletes competing on equal footing with the world's best. The ODI World Cup triumph last year was the first concrete proof. Edgbaston may have been the second.

India's next Group A fixture will determine whether this was a statement of intent or simply the expected result against a weaker opponent. With Australia and South Africa also in the group, the stakes will only rise. But on a grey Sunday in Birmingham, Deepti Sharma made one thing clear: this Indian squad is not here to participate. It is here to win.
nri_angle: India’s dominant T20 World Cup win over Pakistan is the most-watched women’s cricket event among diaspora audiences, and Deepti Sharma’s historic achievement resonates with NRI fans tracking India’s growing dominance in women’s cricket.
